cards.title: The long S
instructions: Sit up, feet flat.
One low breath into the belly — the hand on your stomach moves, the one on your chest does not.
Make a steady 'sssss' and hold it as long as you can, evenly.
Stop when it breaks up or gets louder.
Log the seconds. Compare it with your 'aaah' number — if the S is much longer, your voice is leaking air.

cards.title: Countdown ladder
instructions: One full, low breath.
Count backwards from thirty, out loud, evenly.
The last number must be exactly as loud as the first — that is the whole point.
The moment you feel your throat squeeze, stop.
Log how far down you reached.

cards.title: One breath, one sentence
instructions: Take one low breath.
Say: 'When the meeting finally started, forty minutes late, half the people who needed to be there had already left for lunch.'
Say it in one breath, at a normal speaking volume, without speeding up at the end.
Speeding up at the end means you are running out of air — that is the habit we are breaking.
Log 1 if you made it in one breath, 0 if you didn't.

cards.title: Humming warm-up
instructions: Lips closed, teeth slightly apart, jaw loose.
Hum a comfortable low note. You should feel a buzz on your lips and nose, not in your throat.
Hold for ten seconds, rest, repeat five times.
If you feel it in the throat, go quieter — this drill is about taking the work off the throat.

cards.title: The reset sigh
instructions: In through the nose for four.
A second short sip of air on top.
Long slow sigh out through the mouth, eight counts, jaw loose.
Six rounds. Use this in the two minutes before you have to speak to a room.

cards.title: Low and slow
instructions: Read this out loud at half the speed you think is right: 'I looked at the numbers again this morning.'
Now say it again, quieter, and let the last word land fully.
Do it four times. Each time, quieter and slower than felt comfortable.
This will feel absurdly slow to you and completely normal to a listener. That gap is the thing you are correcting.

cards.title: Ribs, not shoulders
instructions: Put both hands on the sides of your lower ribs, fingers pointing forward.
Breathe in. The ribs should widen sideways under your hands.
If your shoulders rise instead, that is chest breathing — the reason volume ends up coming from your throat.
Ten slow breaths, widening the ribs each time. Shoulders stay still.

cards.title: Staircase counting
instructions: One breath. Count: one — one two — one two three — one two three four, and keep extending.
Return to 'one' at the start of each run and go one number further each time.
Do it all on a single breath, at an even volume.
Log the highest number you reached before running out.
